stem: Two source-water samples have nearly the same pH, but one requires substantially more acid to reach the same adjusted pH. Which interpretation is strongest?
choices: The extra acid demand suggests the sample has lower conductivity and therefore fewer dissolved ions overall
The samples likely differ in alkalinity, so similar pH values did not reflect equal acid-neutralizing capacity
The extra acid demand suggests the sample contains more fertilizer residue from upstream irrigation equipment history
The pH meters are probably drifting differently, so instrument error is the most likely explanation
rationale: Water sources with similar pH can differ in alkalinity. Higher acid-neutralizing capacity can require more acid to produce the same pH change, so pH should not be interpreted alone.
